Long.description: 64-bit signed integer, the default numeric type for integers in Clojure

Double.description: 64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point, the default type for decimal literals

String.description: Immutable sequence of Unicode characters, same as Java strings

Boolean.description: Boolean value type; nil and false are falsy, everything else is truthy

Keyword.description: Interned self-evaluating name, `:k`. Cheap to compare and callable as a map lookup.

Symbol.description: A name referring to something else; what code is written in.

PersistentVector.description: Immutable indexed sequence with effectively O(1) append and lookup, built on a 32-way trie.

PersistentHashMap.description: Immutable hash map with structural sharing. Small maps use PersistentArrayMap, which preserves insertion order.

PersistentList.description: Singly linked list. `conj` prepends; code itself is made of these.

PersistentHashSet.description: Immutable set; also usable as a membership predicate.

LazySeq.description: Sequence realised on demand and cached.

Atom.description: Synchronous uncoordinated reference, updated by compare-and-set.

Ratio.description: Exact rational produced by integer division, e.g. `(/ 1 3)`.

BigInt.description: Arbitrary-precision integer for numbers exceeding Long range

Var.description: A mutable, thread-local-rebindable container for a top-level binding.

IFn.description: Anything callable — functions, keywords, maps, sets, vectors.
